definitions.meaning: The amount of surface a shape covers, found for a rectangle by multiplying its length by its width.
The total distance around the edge of a shape: add the lengths of all its sides.
A shape made by joining simpler shapes, like the L made from part A, 200 by 120, and part B, 120 by 140.
The smallest rectangle that a shape fits inside: for this L it is 200 by 260, but part of the box is empty.

mechanismSteps: Two rectangles make one L: split the L into part A, 200 by 120 with area 24 000, and part B, 120 by 140 with area 16 800.
Trace the edge for the perimeter: walk all six edges - 200, 120, 80, 140, 120 and 260 - and add them to get the perimeter of 920.
Watch out: the missing corner has no area: the 200 by 260 bounding box gives 52 000, but its corner is empty, so that count is too big.
The takeaway: add the areas of the parts for the area, and walk every side for the perimeter.
objectives: Split an L-shape into two rectangles and add their areas to find the total area
Find the perimeter of an L-shape by adding all six edge lengths, including the inner steps
subject: math
title: Area and perimeter of an L-shape

trap.explanation: The eye completes the L into a rectangle and measures the imaginary corner. The empty corner of the L was never filled, so it adds no area; count only what is there. In the animation scene s3 the 200 by 260 box gives 52 000, but the real area is only the two filled parts: 24 000 + 16 800 = 40 800.
trap.misconception: The area of the L-shape is the length times the width of its bounding box.

workedExample: In scene s1, the L splits into part A, 200 by 120, and part B, 120 by 140. Part A has area 200 x 120 = 24 000 and part B has area 120 x 140 = 16 800, so the total area is 24 000 + 16 800 = 40 800.
